answer: Anchor each identity to a weekly jade market in a tundra town: every epoch the operator must attend and sign the market ledger with a quill pen, the entry binding the epoch nonce and a stall photo. One signature, one vote; the ledger exposes any reused signature, which collapses to a single identity and burns a $50 stake. A farm wanting 100 votes must send 100 people to 100 markets each epoch, about $30 travel plus a day of wages each, while an honest operator signs once, free. Cost is priced, protocol-enforced, tied to a body that cannot be split or pre-grown, and rises linearly with n.
